article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Morning Brief
article.dek: Overnight the board re-dealt the Value card to the Raiders, final injury reports ruled Breece Hall out, and three Sunday stadiums look wet.

items.headline: Value re-dealt overnight: Raiders +3.5 is the new +EV card
paragraphs: The morning board dropped the 49ers +3.0 from the Value slot and dealt Raiders +3.5 (-105, FanDuel) instead. That is the model's +EV play on this slate — Las Vegas at New England, Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET.

Nothing about the 49ers game got cheaper for you; the model's read simply moved to a better price. If your book shows a different number on Raiders +3.5, tap Check and run your exact line and price through the evaluator.
items.takeaway: Value is always the +EV card — follow the card, not the team. This morning's card says Raiders +3.5.

items.headline: Final injury reports: Breece Hall out headlines a long Jets\/Browns list
paragraphs: The Jets ruled out running back Breece Hall (quad) for Sunday's home game against Cleveland, along with linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (quad), receiver AD Mitchell (finger) and lineman Dylan Parham (knee). Edge rusher Will McDonald (calf) was added to the report Friday and is questionable; Kingsley Enagbare (knee) practiced fully Friday and is questionable.

Cleveland ruled out defensive tackles Mason Graham (knee, ankle) and Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), lineman Teven Jenkins (back), receiver Tylan Wallace (knee) and tight end Carsen Ryan (calf). Elgton Jenkins, Grant Delpit, Derek Barnett and Mekhi Blackmon carry no designation and will play.

Elsewhere: New Orleans is missing both starting linebackers, Kaden Elliss (calf) and Anfernee Jennings (knee). Minnesota is down left tackle Christian Darrisaw (concussion) and cornerback Charles Demmings (hamstring), with guard Donovan Jackson already out for the season — but Justin Jefferson (ankle) plans to play pending a Saturday check. Tennessee safety Amani Hooker (concussion protocol) is out and rookie receiver Carnell Tate (back) is questionable; Houston receiver Tank Dell (knee) is out. Seattle is without cornerback Julian Neal, linebacker Chazz Surratt and running back Zach Charbonnet; the 49ers' Nick Bosa (calf) misses a third straight game. Indianapolis receiver Keenan Allen (groin) finished Friday as a full participant and should play against Pittsburgh; cornerback Charvarius Ward (groin) did the same. Washington's Jayden Daniels (elbow) is not 100 percent yet but is expected to play; Terry McLaurin (hamstring) will likely be a game-time decision.
Inactives for the 1:00 p.m. ET games are announced about 90 minutes before kickoff — this is the watch list until then.
items.takeaway: Questionable is not out and out is not questionable — but Hall, Bosa, Elliss, Hooker and Darrisaw are already decided. Plan around the outs; check the rest at the inactive deadline.

items.headline: Sunday weather: rain in Washington, Pittsburgh and New Jersey
paragraphs: Final National Weather Service forecasts for the Sunday 1:00 p.m. ET window: Landover (Giants at Commanders) — rain, about 70°F, near-100% chance of rain. Pittsburgh (Colts at Steelers) — showers and thunderstorms, mid-60s, wind 9 to 13 mph. MetLife (Browns at Jets) — rain, mid-60s, 93% chance of rain.

Miami (Bengals at Dolphins) runs hot — low 90s with a slight storm chance. Nashville (Texans at Titans) has about a 50-50 shot of rain. Foxborough (Raiders at Patriots) stays mostly dry, low 60s. Clean: Lambeau (Bears at Packers) sunny near 80°F; Seattle (49ers at Seahawks) sunny, low 60s.
Weather is information, not an edge by itself — note which games could get sloppy, then price your book's total in Check like always.
items.takeaway: Three 1:00 p.m. ET games look wet. File it, don't force it.

items.headline: Quarterback room: no new changes
paragraphs: The app still lists Tyler Huntley as Baltimore's expected starter for Sunday night at Atlanta — the board has priced Lamar Jackson's absence since Friday. Jameis Winston remains the Giants' expected starter; Cam Ward is Tennessee's starter for the early game against Houston.
If a Sunday-morning report changes any of this, the board hasn't seen it yet — check the app before kickoff.
items.takeaway: No new QB news overnight. The contingencies are already in the prices.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Hit Rate stays Minnesota — the likeliest winner, not the best price
paragraphs: Minnesota moneyline is -134 on FanDuel, a touch cheaper than last night's -136. The model's own number on the Vikings is far higher — that gap is why this card is about winning the bet, not beating the price. The app's tutorial says it straight: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
items.takeaway: Play Hit Rate when you want the card most likely to cash.

items.headline: Balanced: Chicago moneyline -124
paragraphs: Chicago moneyline moved from -122 to -124 on FanDuel overnight. The model gives the Bears about a 57% chance at Green Bay — the middle ground between chasing winners and chasing prices.
items.takeaway: Balanced is the starting point if you're new — a strong pick without paying too much.

items.headline: Value: always the model's +EV play — this morning it's Raiders +3.5
paragraphs: Raiders +3.5 at -105 on FanDuel carries the only plus-expected-value tag on the board this morning. That is what the Value card means, every single day: the model thinks the price beats fair.
items.takeaway: +EV is a property of the price, not the team. When the card changes, the play changes.

items.headline: Handle vs. tickets — reading a betting split
paragraphs: Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: imagine 100 bets are placed on a game. 75 of the tickets are on Team A, but 60% of the total dollars are on Team B. The tickets say the crowd likes A; the money says the average bet on B is much bigger.

A gap like that can mean sharper money is on B — or it can mean a few big public bets landed on B. The split is a question, not an answer: it tells you where to look next (line movement, other books) before you decide what it means.
items.takeaway: When you see tickets and money disagree, don't pick a side from the split alone — use it as one more layer around the card's price.

items.headline: Value re-deal: 49ers +3.0 off, Raiders +3.5 on
paragraphs: Last night's board had the 49ers +3.0 in the Value slot; this morning's board has Raiders +3.5 (-105, FanDuel). The card changed because the price edge moved — San Francisco at Seattle no longer clears the model's bar, Las Vegas at New England does.
items.takeaway: Cards are re-dealt every refresh. Bet the card in front of you, not yesterday's.

items.headline: Chicago -122 to -124; Minnesota -136 to -134
paragraphs: Small overnight moves on the two moneyline cards: Chicago got two cents more expensive on FanDuel (-122 to -124; DraftKings shows -125), Minnesota got two cents cheaper (-136 to -134; DraftKings shows -142). Both cards stayed supported and both stayed bets.
items.takeaway: Two cents is noise, not news — but the card follows the price.

items.headline: The books split on Steelers-Colts; Ravens-Falcons settle at -3.5
paragraphs: DraftKings has Pittsburgh -3.0 while FanDuel still shows -2.5 — same game, different number, and that half point is exactly what last night's hook lesson was about. Ravens-Falcons is -3.5 at both books now (DraftKings -102, FanDuel even money) after Friday's move.

If your book's number isn't the card's number, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet\/no-bet verdict on your price — a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: Your book's line is the only line that matters. Check it.

items.headline: Saturday job: build your Sunday shopping list now
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening. Pull the three card prices — Vikings -134, Bears -124, Raiders +3.5 — from your own book this morning and compare. Anything that doesn't match the card price goes through Check before you touch it.
items.takeaway: Shop the price before the game, not during it.

items.headline: Log the losers too
paragraphs: Settlement is manual — there's no auto-settle, so the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. Winners log themselves. Log the losers the night they happen, while the receipt is still on your phone.
items.takeaway: An honest tracker is the only one worth keeping.

evidence.fact: Fade attempt Saturday ~6:15 a.m. Denver. The VSiN betting-splits page was fetched as text (visible free row was CFB Friday's game, Florida State vs Louisville — not usable) and a live-browser read of the NFL tab returned the free featured row: Sunday's Eagles@Jaguars (PHI +7.5 / JAX -7.5, total 41.5, PHI +310 / JAX -395). Spread: JAX 51% bets / 64% handle (no side disagreement). Total: same row leads both. Moneyline: 75% of tickets on JAX but 53% of handle on PHI — a tickets-vs-handle disagreement, but DraftKings-only, with no line movement shown.
evidence.interpretation: The moneyline tickets/handle disagreement is real but DK-only splits alone are insufficient and no corroborating line movement or second book was observed, so it does not qualify as a Fade; per the rules, no Fade is manufactured.
evidence.app_guidance: Learning substitute used in the fade slot.
